arxiv-2603-10313: Kristy A Carpenter and co-authors test whether large language models can tell real opioid slang from harmless uses of the same words on social media. Words like smack and blues often mean other things, so simple word lists flag far too much. Four leading models were tried with a lexicon, without one, and on simulated new slang. Each model beat the best lexicon strategy by a wide margin, with higher recall as well. The authors say such tools can clean data for work on low-prevalence topics.
arxiv-2603-10413: Nasim Soltani and co-authors build a multilayer defense to keep machine learning based network intrusion detection systems safe from adversarial attacks. Such attacks can fool detectors with crafted traffic, so the team generated hostile examples with a GAN and with the fast gradient sign method. Their defense stacks classifiers in a first layer, then checks benign calls with an autoencoder in a second layer, and adds adversarial training. On two standard datasets, the approach raised resilience against these attacks.
arxiv-2603-10613: Yuji Chen and co-authors create MUNIChus, the first multilingual benchmark for news image captioning, covering nine languages including low-resource Sinhala and Urdu. News captions must blend article text with the image itself, and past work is mostly English for lack of data. The team evaluated leading neural captioning models on the new set, with more than twenty models already benchmarked. Captioning news images stayed hard across languages. The public benchmark is meant to open room for better multilingual models and fairer tests of them.
arxiv-2603-10713: Evgeny Kushnir and co-authors propose a probabilistic framework, PV-VASM, for checking the robustness of voice anti-spoofing models. Speech synthesis now lets adversaries impersonate speakers and reach sensitive resources, while most detectors lack formal guarantees and fail on unseen generators. PV-VASM estimates the chance of misclassification under text-to-speech, voice cloning, and signal changes. The approach works for any model, covers unseen generators, and comes with a proved upper bound on error probability. Tests across diverse settings support it as a practical verification tool.
arxiv-2603-10913: Parishad BehnamGhader and coauthors propose LLM2Vec-Gen. It builds text embeddings inside a large language model's own output space. It does not discard that space through contrastive fine-tuning. Trainable special tokens learn to compress the model's likely response. They compress it into a fixed-length vector. An embedding teacher guides this step. A reconstruction goal guides it too, while the backbone stays frozen. The embeddings top self-supervised benchmark scores. They inherit safety and reasoning traits. They can also be decoded back into readable text.
arxiv-2603-11313: Julieta Bollati, Mariela Olguín, and Domingo Tarzia discretize optimization problems tied to steady heat conduction. The two systems differ in one boundary condition: fixed temperature versus convective exchange. Each system carries three problems, over the heat source, the boundary flux, and the outside temperature. On a domain, the answers are already known. Using finite differences, they obtain explicit discrete answers. They prove error estimates as the mesh refines and the convection coefficient grows. They confirm the theory in tests.
arxiv-2603-11513: Pandey asks whether small language models can actually use the passages they retrieve. Retrieval-augmented generation promises better factual accuracy, yet small models may ignore the help. Five model sizes, from 360M to 8B, face three families and four retrieval setups. A knowledge split sorts questions into known ones and ones needing outside facts. Even with oracle retrieval, models at 7B or below miss most answers they could not give alone. Added context wipes out many once-known answers, and the top failure is ignoring the passage outright.
arxiv-2603-12213: Kumar and co-authors ask how magnetoacoustic shocks distort magnetic field readings in the solar chromosphere. Umbral flashes signal such shocks, and their effect on inferred field oscillations stayed unclear. Five sunspots near disk center were watched with the GREGOR telescope and inverted with HAZEL2. One-component models split the spots: three show stronger fields with the shocks, two show sharp drops. Two-slab models fit the profiles just as well with a constant field, blaming steep velocity gradients instead. The paper weighs both readings with care.
arxiv-2603-12413: Šesták, Heczko, Straka, Sozinov, and Zelený compute how doping reshapes twin formation in Ni-Mn-Ga martensite. Density functional theory gives planar fault energy curves for a key shear system. Pure Ni2MnGa faces doped supercells with copper, cobalt, iron, or zinc on varied sublattices. Some swaps lower the nucleation barrier and soften the profile, easing twin growth. Others raise barriers and hinder twinning, even when they stabilize the martensite phase. The nanotwin minimum depth also links dopant choice to modulation stability in their results.
arxiv-2603-12513: Kim, Hu, Kuo, and Beerel present MemRoPE, a training-free way to generate very long videos. Sliding-window caches in autoregressive diffusion drop past context, causing drift and stale motion. MemRoPE compresses all past keys into memory tokens with long-term and short-term streams. Exponential moving averages keep global identity and recent dynamics inside a fixed-size cache. Online RoPE indexing stores unrotated keys and adds position codes at attention time. Tests show steadier motion, sharper frames, and more stable subjects over runs up to hour scale.
arxiv-2603-12613: Ankit Kumar and Hajime Sotani build a relativistic framework for slowly rotating neutron stars made of two fluids. The two parts interact only through gravity, each conserved on its own. From the coupled frame-dragging equations, they define a total moment of inertia set by the background star. The system shows two collective spin modes with distinct eigen-moments. Applied to stars with dark matter, results show that dark-sector details, not mere presence, decide if spin-tidal links hold.
arxiv-2603-12713: Jiguang Yu and co-authors link microscopic cell damage to macroscopic tissue balance in stem cell systems. Tissues must hold steady while damage builds up in single cells. Their model starts from a structured partial differential equation for cell states. Under uniform mortality, they reduce it exactly to a low-dimensional system. Homeostasis then acts as a Nash equilibrium, with growth rates of stem and mature cells equal. A mouse gut crypt case study matches observed repair after irradiation.
arxiv-2603-13113: The ATLAS Collaboration reports the first search for Higgs boson pairs made with a top-quark pair at the Large Hadron Collider. The data cover 196 inverse femtobarns at two collision energies. Three decay final states were targeted, rich in b-quarks, leptons, or photons. The measured rate came out below the standard model value, with wide errors. A 95% confidence limit caps the rate at 20 times the standard model prediction. A related field theory coefficient was also bounded.
arxiv-2603-13413: Rodrigo Siqueira and Danilo Monteiro Ribeiro ask software staff how to improve corporate training in their field. Tech firms spend on staff growth, yet learning often fails to transfer to project work. Their study reads 174 open-ended replies with reflexive thematic analysis. Five themes came out of what staff suggested. They cover practical fit, course quality, time and job conditions, incentives, and mentoring. Gains need joined fixes across practice, support, and culture, they conclude.
arxiv-2603-13913: Frittaion and Genovesi show that a weak set theory with Axiom Beta proves elementary transfinite recursion. The theory, called C, can build the relativized constructible hierarchy for every set. It matches Simpson's ATR0-set system without the Axiom of Countability. The theory also proves that the Veblen function and all primitive recursive set functions are total. A variant with rudimentary-function closure instead of the finite powerset axiom turns out strictly weaker.
arxiv-2603-14013: Ans, Zamkotsian, and Demésy design blazed metasurface gratings that shops can actually make. Their 3D design method works for light in the visible and near-infrared bands, in reflection. A freeform design reaches an average diffraction score near 62 percent, but its shapes are hard to build. A pillar-based design adds making limits to the search, such as e-beam writing and ion etching. It still reaches about 57 percent, with low dependence on polarization.
arxiv-2603-14113: Zhu and co-authors study how hydrogen enters the barriers of aluminum Josephson junctions, a source of qubit variability. They pair molecular dynamics of aluminum oxidation in oxygen and water vapor with atomistic quantum transport math. Across 400 samples, the count of trapped hydrogen atoms follows a beta-binomial spread. Most hydrogen sits near the barrier surface in Al-OH forms. The predicted Josephson energy lands near 10 gigahertz, and hydrogen shifts its mean by about 11 percent.
arxiv-2603-14213: Shang and co-authors trace how heat moves through the three phases of MgAgSb, a thermoelectric material. First-principles math shows lattice heat flow rising from the alpha to the beta to the gamma phase. Four-phonon scattering cuts the particle-like part in the beta and gamma phases. The wave-like part, from coherent phonon tunneling, peaks in the complex alpha phase at up to 44 percent of the total. Heat trends with temperature differ by phase, which the authors tie to these split paths.
arxiv-2603-14413: Shi, Zhang, and Liu study particle orbits and gravitational waveforms around black holes in bumblebee gravity. This Einstein variant breaks Lorentz symmetry through a coupling set by one parameter. The authors work out geodesics and the effective potential for charged and uncharged holes. Charge and the Lorentz-breaking parameter widen the space of bound orbits. Periodic orbits are sorted by whirl, zoom, and vertex counts. The uncharged case matches Schwarzschild in its static potential, yet its orbit shapes differ in clear ways.
arxiv-2603-15013: Liu and co-authors build CycleRL, a sim-to-real framework that teaches a bicycle to ride itself. A policy trained with proximal policy optimization maps sensor input straight to control actions in NVIDIA Isaac Sim. Rewards cover balance, speed tracking, and steering. Domain randomization varies the setup so the policy copes with real-world mismatch. In simulation it reports a 99.90 percent balance success rate, and the team also ran it on real hardware.
arxiv-2603-15713: Sakhno and co-authors bridge a gap between learned embeddings and handcrafted features. Finance systems run on event sequences like transactions and user actions. Shop-floor pipelines still trust hand-built stats for clarity and speed. Learned embeddings hold rich signals but stay hard to read. Their EAFD framework pairs pretrained embeddings with an LLM feature agent. The agent proposes features, then scores each one twice. Alignment checks what embeddings already hold. Complementarity hunts signals they miss. Gains reached 5.8 percent over top embeddings.
arxiv-2603-15813: Müller revisits Jordan's 1878 bound on finite linear groups. Jordan showed each such group holds an abelian normal subgroup. The quotient size is bounded by dimension alone, with no explicit number given. Blichfeldt later found an explicit bound by representation methods. Bieberbach gave a geometric proof, which Frobenius then simplified. Müller presents a cleaned, self-contained form of Frobenius's argument. The streamlined proof yields a quotient bound of 25 to the n squared. The note keeps the full chain in one place.
arxiv-2603-15913: Shvydka, Karpov, and Gupta explain the FLASH sparing effect through tissue structure. FLASH therapy fires radiation at ultra-high dose rates in brief bursts. Tumor kill stays strong while healthy tissue takes less harm. The pair of responses may split on recombination rates, they argue. Ordered healthy tissue packs charges densely under radiation. An electron-hole liquid then forms and slows radical growth. Disordered tumor tissue drains energy fast and breeds radicals instead. Dose and dose-rate thresholds for the effect follow.
arxiv-2603-16013: Yu and co-authors draft safety case patterns for language-driven driving systems. Vision-language-action drivers read scenes, words, and act in one loop. Open-ended instructions can steer such drivers toward unsafe moves. Their RAISE approach tailors safety cases to instruction-based systems. A widened hazard analysis spells safe scenes and outcomes. Set patterns then structure the safety claims and evidence. A SimLingo case study shows the method in action. The goal is rigorous trust for a new driver class.
arxiv-2603-16613: Gyenizse, Maróti, and Zádori ask when kinds of graph connectedness must coincide. A digraph can be weakly, strongly, or extremely connected. Each notion uses a different grade of path. The team studies digraphs compatible with algebras in a class. With a Hobby-McKenzie polymorphism, strong and extreme parts coincide. The converse also holds across a whole equational class. One payoff: n-permutability matches extreme connectedness of weak parts.
arxiv-2603-16713: Cameron and Blackwell compare how three timbre autoencoders organize their latent spaces. One model is unsupervised; one takes the 19 word labels as conditions. The third takes continuous perceptual features from the AudioCommons models. All train on the team's labeled guitar dataset. Perceptual conditioning gave the most compact, pitch-stable space. One-hot word conditioning lagged on several structure metrics. The study supplies tools for judging timbre latent spaces. Controllable, readable audio generation is the end goal.
arxiv-2603-17013: Tagliente sets out to produce infinitely many exotic smooth structures on a class of 4-manifolds. The manifolds are smooth, closed, and oriented. Their fundamental group is the infinite dihedral group. Exotic structures are distinct smooth structures on one and the same topological manifold. The construction assumes the second Betti numbers b2+ and b2- are both at least 12. The result adds to the small stock of manifolds known to carry infinitely many exotic structures.
arxiv-2603-17313: Gell-Redman and co-authors compute how long Brownian motion takes, on average, to first escape from curved surfaces of two kinds. The surfaces carry either asymptotically hyperbolic metrics or gas giant metrics, cut off near a boundary. For the hyperbolic case, the mean escape time grows like minus log epsilon as the cutoff shrinks. For gas giant metrics, it stays bounded instead. The authors explain the contrast with the theory of polyhomogeneous conormal functions. They confirm both results with Monte Carlo simulations.
arxiv-2603-17513: Lee, Fang, and Chang design a proof-of-authorship scheme for diffusion-made content. A creator picks the generation seed and binds it to their identity with cryptography. Only the true creator can later prove the link, they argue. Watermarks and timestamps prove mere possession, which anyone could claim first. A probabilistic judge scores how likely a claim is false. Tests use Stable Diffusion 2.1 and XL under several attacks.
arxiv-2603-17913: Kessinger and Martinez-Finkelshtein solve a weighted equilibrium problem on the interval from minus one to one. A uniform background charge on the same interval sets the outside field. A single dial, tau, scales that field up or down. For each tau they give the equilibrium measure, its support, and its key transforms in closed form. Three regimes appear as tau grows, they show. Support runs from one inner cut, to the full interval, to two outer cuts.
arxiv-2603-18013: Shigemura reports a gap between what large language models learn and what they express in normal output. Across 300 generations from three models and ten tasks, no non-causal solution frames appeared at all. Yet the same content could be drawn out under set extraction conditions. The study covers both story and advice tasks. It suggests that task-shaped generation rules can fully suppress learned content.
arxiv-2603-18713: Seoane, Oianguren-Asua, Solé, and Oriols reply to a claim that realistic views of weak values must clash. Aredes and Saldanha had argued that such views lead to inconsistency in general. The commenters accept the clashes for the weak values studied there. They deny that the general argument is sound, calling it formally incorrect. Bohmian mechanics serves as the counterexample. Weak values postselected in position can act as system properties inside that frame, cut loose from the measuring device, in a consistent way.
arxiv-2603-18813: Chen and Jiang ask whether language models can propose good new math research problems. Their agent works in differential geometry and writes problems meant to be unknown. It produced 665 candidate research problems. Human experts then checked the list by hand. Many problems were new to the experts and carried real research value, the authors report. The study builds on their earlier criteria and benchmark for machine mathematical creativity. It shifts the test from solving known problems to posing fresh ones worth study.
arxiv-2603-18913: Sevilla argues that turbulence has a simple hidden backbone. The stress that makes turbulence hard to close comes from non-local effects in the flow laws. He shows that this response can be shrunk to a small set of changing values. The shrunk system acts like a damped oscillator. The lead swirl mode feeds energy to finer modes. Known traits then follow from one structure. These include mid-range scaling, shear-driven spread, and the log-shaped speed profile near walls.
arxiv-2603-19113: Cai and co-authors give a stable, fast solver for sound scattering off many bodies. For each body, they compute a sharp local map of how it scatters sound. Those maps join into one global linear system. The global matrix stays well behaved even with very many bodies. Fast methods can speed the matrix steps for iterative solvers. The local maps may use an ill-set method that is simple to code. The global solve stays stable and scales well, they show, in two and three dimensions.
arxiv-2603-19213: Baum and Laux sort out the blurred terms for human roles in AI systems. They draw the line by cause, not by where a person sits in a loop. In-the-loop help is part of what makes the output, so it is constitutive. On-the-loop help sits outside that chain and can block or change outputs, so it is corrective. They split the second role by timing and by how minds combine. Legal oversight, they argue, needs real readiness to step in.
arxiv-2603-19513: Moreira and co-authors study quantum state transfer in one-dimensional high-root topological insulators. These chains can hold several domains and many edge states in distinct energy gaps. That allows multiple transfer processes in a single model, of use for multiplexing. The team derives how transfer times relate across root models and gaps. Splitting a chain into domains slows transfer, but fidelity stays high. More domain wall states raise fidelity under disorder, thanks to topological protection.
arxiv-2603-19613: Liang and co-authors present OrbitNVS, a method that makes new views of a 3D object from few known views. Prior methods struggle with unseen regions, above all from a single view. OrbitNVS reframes the task as orbit video generation. A pretrained video model supplies rich visual priors for the synthesis. Camera adapters give accurate control of the moving viewpoint. A normal map branch guides geometry, and pixel-space supervision fights blur. On GSO and OmniObject3D, it beats prior methods, gaining about 3 dB PSNR in single-view tests.
arxiv-2603-20113: Lowack derives a theory of dendritic crack growth in ceramic solid state batteries. Above a critical current, metal dendrites pierce the ceramic electrolyte while plating. A dendrite grows when cracking the ceramic costs less energy than the detour current wastes as heat. This least dissipation principle drives Lowack's analytic result. The critical current scales with the longest thin defect to the power three halves. Sample scatter should then follow a Weibull distribution. Its modulus is smaller than the one for ceramic tensile strength.
arxiv-2603-20213: Yuan and co-authors build AgenticGEO, a self evolving system for generative engine optimization. Generative search answers questions by synthesis, so content aims at inclusion, not ranking. Static heuristics and one prompt tuning overfit to one engine's habits. Their framework treats optimization as a control problem shaped by the content itself. A MAP-Elites archive evolves a diverse set of compositional strategies. A co evolving critic stands in for the engine to cut feedback costs. The system targets stronger intrinsic content quality, which should hold up as engines change.
arxiv-2603-20413: Mennickent and co-authors track light cycles in the eclipsing binary OGLE-LMC-DPV-062. Many close binaries vary on cycles far longer than their orbits. Such cycles likely trace changes in the accretion disk. They study 32.3 years of OGLE and MACHO photometry for this system. The orbital period is 6.904858 days, with a long cycle of 229.7 days. They model the disk at 20 phases across the long cycle. MESA models help pin down the system's evolutionary state. Quasi-conservative mass transfer, though, gives rates that look too high.
arxiv-2603-20513: Korikov and Sanner present ReBOL, a search method that uses Bayesian optimization to find relevant documents. Standard LLM reranking can only reorder the top hits from vector search. Good documents outside that set stay lost. ReBOL starts with LLM made query rewrites to seed a relevance model. It then picks batches of documents for the LLM to score. Each scored batch updates the model for the next round. On five BEIR datasets ReBOL beat LLM reranker baselines on recall. On Robust04 it reached 46.5 percent recall at 100, versus 35.0.
arxiv-2603-21013: Studerus and co-authors build an open framework that gives the Pepper robot fast, multimodal interaction with a language model. Many Pepper setups chain speech to text, a model, and text to speech, which adds delay and loses tone cues. Their framework uses end to end speech to speech models instead. Function calling lets the model plan robot actions, such as navigation, gaze, and tablet use. It also folds in vision, touch, and system state. The code runs on the robot's tablet or a plain Android device.
arxiv-2603-21113: Korotyaev studies wave scattering for an operator H. The operator is a free part plus a potential that acts with unequal strength in each direction. The free part need not be elliptic, which makes the case more general than usual. He shows the wave operators exist and are complete. The operator has no singular continuous spectrum, and its eigenvalues can pile up only at zero. With stronger limits on the potential, it has only finitely many eigenvalues. The results also cover time dependent potentials.
arxiv-2603-21213: Xia and co-authors propose Positional Seg-CFT, a way to make counterfactual images that change one region at a time. Such images help with data augmentation, bias checks, and disease modeling. Past segmentor guided fine tuning could change only global traits of a whole structure. Their method splits each structure into regional segments. It measures each region on its own, so edits can stay local and still look anatomically sound. On coronary CT angiography, the edits look realistic and track how disease progresses.
arxiv-2603-21713: Plessen presents a simple method to smooth flight paths for unmanned aerial vehicles. The method builds on a Dubins airplane model of the craft's motion. A decoupling step yields direct control laws for flight path angle and speed. Only roll angle control needs an optimization step, and that step is a small linear program. Two variants differ in how they track a reference centerline and shape the path. Plessen also outlines extensions to aerobatic flight and to tractor path planning over 3D terrain. Simulations validate the approach.
arxiv-2603-21813: Nies and Parra build a theory of extended plasma modes in fusion devices with very low magnetic shear. Standard theory treats passing electrons as instant responders. At low shear, ion-scale modes stretch far along the field, and that shortcut breaks. Their multiscale expansion of the gyrokinetic equation yields a new mode, the geodesic extended mode. It couples the slow response of both electrons and ions. Tests against gyrokinetic simulations support the theory, and they map how the mode shifts with plasma settings.
arxiv-2603-21913: Lee and Kim schedule speeds for many agents on fixed routes without collisions. Since paths cannot change, they optimize when each agent passes its waypoints. A smooth surrogate model turns those timings into position curves and captures tracking lag. Safety comes from distance penalties checked on a dense time grid. An ADMM solver with inexact projections alternates timing updates with gradient steps that push agents apart. In random-crossing, bottleneck, and network tests, it found feasible schedules and beat a hierarchical baseline on bottleneck finish times.
arxiv-2603-22213: Tang and co-authors propose SPA, a plain baseline for injecting new knowledge into language models. Models still lack coverage in narrow, data-scarce fields. SPA uses a small set of hand-designed prompts to generate large synthetic training sets. In systematic comparisons, SPA beats several strong baselines. RL-based methods gain token efficiency at small scale but lose diversity as data grows. Multi-stage prompting wins only until simple prompts are tuned with care. Careful prompt design plus scale, they conclude, is hard to beat.
arxiv-2603-22913: Suzuki, Qi, and Inaba build a multilingual counseling dialogue dataset by translation. Good counseling datasets are scarce and hard to share. They translate the Japanese KokoroChat corpus into English and Chinese. No single model gives the best translation for every input, they note. Their ensemble method first collects drafts from several models. One model then merges them, using a review of each draft's strengths and flaws. Human raters preferred the ensemble output over any single top model. The dataset is released in public.
arxiv-2603-23513: Vaid and ten co-authors built Berta, an open-source AI scribe for clinical notes. Paid scribes cost far more per doctor, hide how they work, and keep data outside the hospital. Berta pairs speech recognition with language models inside Alberta Health Services' own cloud. Over eight months, 198 emergency doctors in 105 sites logged more than 22,000 sessions. Use climbed from 680 to 5,530 sessions a month. Running costs stayed under 30 dollars per doctor monthly. The service now expands toward 850 doctors.
arxiv-2603-23613: Ravi and four co-authors present LLMLOOP, a framework that polishes model-written code and tests in rounds. Language models draft code fast, but drafts often fail to compile or run wrong. LLMLOOP runs five repair loops over each draft. The loops fix compile errors, static warnings, and failing tests in turn. A mutation loop then grades and hardens the test suite itself. The polished tests double as a regression suite for the code. On the HUMANEVAL-X bench, the loops lift output quality by a clear margin.
arxiv-2603-23713: Handley and 18 co-authors launch the SLOPE survey of spin-orbit angles for small planets. A star's spin tilt against a planet's orbit records how the system moved and settled. Giant planets gave easy reads, but small ones mirror the true dynamics better. The Keck Planet Finder measured four new sub-Saturn planets. All four line up with their stars' equators. Pooling such worlds, compact multi-planet packs look strongly aligned. One new world also gains firm planet status from its tilt read.
arxiv-2603-24113: Haag and co-authors implement a feedback-control optimizer on a mixed-signal neuromorphic chip. On-chip learning matters for adaptive neuromorphic systems, but many training rules are hard to build in hardware. In an in-the-loop setup, they train a single-layer spiking network on chip. Tasks cover binary classification and the nonlinear Yin-Yang problem. Chip training matches simulation results and gradient-based baselines, they report. The work shows feedback-driven online learning can run under real mixed-signal limits, a step toward self-adaptive silicon.
arxiv-2603-24213: Taleb and co-authors show that time series imputation models can leak their training data. Such models fill gaps in health, sensor, and finance data. Their attack has two stages. A new membership inference attack uses a reference model to tell which records were in training, even for models that resist overfitting-based attacks. A second attack infers sensitive attributes of the training data, a first for this setting. The membership attack also predicts when attribute inference will work, with 90 percent precision in their tests.
arxiv-2603-24713: Yeshwanth and Dai introduce the task of lookalike object detection in indoor 3D scenes. Repeated objects are a rich but overlooked cue in real scenes. The task classifies object pairs as identical, similar, or different, from multiview images. Their Lookalike3D model is a multiview image transformer that draws on strong priors from large image foundation models. To support the task, they built 3DTwins, a dataset of 76,000 hand-annotated pairs from ScanNet++. The method improves IoU by 104 percent over baselines and helps downstream reconstruction and part co-segmentation.
arxiv-2603-25113: El Zein and Mortada study how local cycle length shapes packing colorings of sparse cubic graphs. In an S-packing coloring, same-color vertices must sit farther apart than their color value allows. They focus on subcubic graphs where degree-3 vertices touch few peers of the same degree. Local girth gives the shortest cycle through a vertex. The pair shows how saturation and local girth jointly fix which packing sequences work. Sharp examples prove the bounds are tight. Open cases are listed for later work.
arxiv-2603-25213: Erdönmez and Yilmaz locate a molecule sender in a vessel-like channel from the spread of its signal. Molecular links could serve health tools, but finding the sender is hard without knowing when it fired. Prior fixes need the send time or many close receivers. Their method uses the time variance of the received pulse near its peak. A Gaussian fit near the peak yields a simple formula that ties spread to distance. In capillary-scale simulations, the distance error lands near one percent.
arxiv-2603-25413: Zhu and co-authors test whether gravity's strength has drifted, using the neutron star merger GW170817. A changing G would dent the strong equivalence idea at relativity's core. They build a wave model where G shifts slowly, in the binary's motion and in the wave's trip through space. Light-based facts from the partner flash pin down distance, spot, and tilt. A joint Bayesian fit then splits drift effects from look-alikes. No drift appears, and the bound on its rate is the tightest yet from real waves.
arxiv-2603-25613: Öztürk, Shahreza, and Marcel benchmark demographic fairness in face verification by multimodal language models. They test nine open models from six families on the IJB-C and RFW protocols. The models range from two to eight billion parameters. Scores cover four ethnicity groups and two gender groups. The authors measure error rates and four fairness metrics based on false matches. They report that FaceLLM-8B, the only face-focused model, beats the general models by a wide margin. Bias patterns differ from those in classic face recognition.
arxiv-2603-25813: Kim and Park present MAGNET, a system that grows expert language models on ordinary hardware without central control. MAGNET joins four parts. An autoresearch pipeline makes datasets, tunes settings, and iterates on errors by itself. BitNet ternary training lets models run on CPUs with no GPU. DiLoCo-based merging combines domain specialists with low communication cost. An on-chain ledger tracks who contributed what. Case studies cover video safety sorting, crypto price direction, and BitNet tuning. The authors report accuracy gains in each study.
arxiv-2603-25913: Chen and Chu derive new summation formulae for binomial moments. They examine four classes of such moments. Their method joins a telescoping trick with an algebraic relation. From this pairing they get several explicit closed forms. The note is short and stays close to the identities themselves. It adds exact formulas for sums that involve binomial terms. Such sums come up often in work on probability and counting.
arxiv-2603-26013: Bagheri Nezhad argues that multilingual NLP must be grounded in culture, not just language coverage. He reviews over fifty papers on multilingual gaps, transfer, and culture-aware testing. Coverage of training data matters, but so do tokenization and prompt language. Translated benchmarks and who validates the data also shape results. He proposes that systems model communicative ecologies instead. These are the institutions, scripts, and communities where language lives. His agenda calls for representation audits, community checks, and living cultural resources.
arxiv-2603-26113: Zhang and co-authors present the first audio-visual method for splitting film sound into its parts. Cinematic separation breaks a mix into speech, music, and effects for dubbing or remastering. Past methods listen only to the audio. Their method treats the task as conditional generation with flow matching. Visual cues guide which sounds belong where. Since no real dataset has isolated tracks, they synthesize training pairs from wild audio and video. A dual-stream visual encoder fits this setup. The model transfers well to real films, they report.
arxiv-2603-26313: Mozes and Prigan prove that exact distances in planar graphs can be stored almost for free. A distance oracle answers the exact gap between any two vertices of a weighted directed planar graph. Past builds with near-linear space and fast queries took much longer to construct. Their method builds the oracle in near-linear time and space. Queries then return exact distances in near polylog time, with no real trade-off among build time, query time, and size.
arxiv-2603-26413: Auvinen and co-authors speed up Bayesian analysis of heavy ion collisions with a deep neural network. Their global fit runs relativistic viscous hydrodynamics with dynamic freeze-out and EKRT initial states. The fit holds over a dozen free parameters for QCD matter and the initial state. Data come from gold, lead, and xenon collisions at RHIC and the LHC. Networks replace the costly simulations, letting the team add flow measures that demand high statistics, and the data favour a specific shear viscosity.
arxiv-2603-26813: Cosso asks whether a generative model built for fast simulation can sharpen coarse calorimeter images. This thesis re-implements a conditional normalizing flow model from an earlier study. The model trains on the CaloChallenge 2022 dataset, based on a Geant4 detector geometry. The goal is superresolution: recovering fine detail from coarse readouts. That would cut computing and hardware costs in particle physics. A strict statistical framework then tests how well outputs match reference data.
arxiv-2603-27413: Jungherr and Rauchfleisch test how people judge AI-driven political outreach. They ran a preregistered study in the US and UK. Each country had 1,800 people. The study varied outreach aim and sender type. Persuasive outreach drew a clear penalty in both countries. People found it less fair and more of a threat. AI-sent outreach drew its own penalty. People doubted that machines should send such messages. The authors warn that public judgment may shape campaign practice.
arxiv-2603-27613: Zhou hunts exact formulas for Stokes constants of anharmonic oscillators. He works out up to 1,200 series terms at 300-digit precision. A sequence speedup step sharpens the raw ratios. The PSLQ method then guesses closed forms from the digits. Three new exact results emerge for higher orders. A known quartic case is confirmed too. Wide searches find no closed form for the rest. That null result is reported with care.
arxiv-2603-28113: Kuang and three co-authors ask why checking a neural network's Lipschitz constant is so hard. That constant bounds how much outputs can change, which matters for robustness. They argue the root trouble is reachability: knowing which hidden states can occur is NP-hard. This blindness forces semidefinite methods to fail in the same ways as the naive layer-by-layer bound. They also show some naive-bound failures come from fixable parameter choices, and sketch bias-free trigonometric layers that make the simple bound tight.
arxiv-2603-28213: Platzgummer, McCrae, and Ahmadi examine how generative AI treats non-standard language, from South Tyrolean dialects to Kurdish varieties. Language models favor standard forms, a bias rooted in older standardization drives. The authors pair sociolinguistic critique with a technical look at fixes. They ask what it would take for models to handle dialects well, and whether doing so can serve fairer, decolonial language policy. The paper blends both lenses to frame the stakes.
arxiv-2603-28513: Pentland and co-authors release a pulse design tool for tokamak plasma control, built on the FreeGSNKE solver. The tool couples an evolving equilibrium solver to a virtual control system with swappable controllers. Users set target waveforms, and the system steers plasma current, position, and shape within coil safety limits. It runs on any machine and supports scenario design, control tuning, and uncertainty studies. On MAST Upgrade shots, its output matched the real discharge data closely.
arxiv-2603-28613: Mareen and co-authors introduce TGIF2, an extended dataset and benchmark for text-guided inpainting forgery. Generative inpainting is a strong editing tool and a growing forensic problem. Earlier tests localized spliced edits but struggled on fully regenerated images. TGIF2 adds edits from FLUX.1 models and random non-semantic masks. Their tests span forgery localization and synthetic image detection. Both kinds of method got worse on FLUX.1 edits. Fine-tuning helped localization on regenerated images, but masks revealed object bias. Generative super-resolution also weakened forensic traces a lot.
arxiv-2603-28813: Marandi studies how debate protocol choices affect quality in multi-agent debate systems. Marandi compares three protocols against a no-interaction baseline. Agents in one setup see only current-round contributions, while another gives full prior-round context. A new rank-based version reorders agents and silences one per round via a judge model. In a macroeconomic case study with 20 events, the rank-based one converged fastest. The no-interaction baseline gave the highest argument diversity. Protocol design clearly matters.
arxiv-2603-29313: Yazdan Parast and co-authors present HSFM, a meta-learning method for robust image classification. Networks often lean on spurious features that fail under shift. Much of the fault may sit in the classifier head, not the backbone. Their method edits features on the support side of a bilevel loop. After a few inner updates, the head should do better on hard examples. Worst-group performance is the target. Training takes minutes on one GPU. Visualizations show the edits track spurious attributes.
arxiv-2603-29913: Altamura and co-authors present SISA, a chip layout that speeds up matrix multiplication. Large language models lean on such operations, but their skewed matrices waste square systolic arrays. SISA splits the square array into horizontal rectangular slabs. Slabs can be scheduled on their own for small or skewed shapes. The full array still runs as one for large jobs. Tests show up to 8.52 times speedup. Energy-delay product falls by 93 percent.
arxiv-2604-00213: Goel and six colleagues test WISE mid-infrared color selection for obscured Type 2 active galactic nuclei at low redshift, using 360,000 SDSS galaxies. K-correction proves essential against contamination, after which a simple W1-W2 above 0.5 cut emerges as optimal for purity and completeness. Even so, that cut catches only about 13 percent of Seyfert 2 galaxies, and reaching it requires the AGN to supply over 75 percent of infrared luminosity. Mid-infrared selection stays incomplete, yet it picks out optically inconspicuous AGNs with low-mass bulges, where most read as star-forming.
arxiv-2604-00413: Booth and colleagues reach deep super-resolution without saturation or stochastic switching of emitters. Most methods lean on those tricks, which slow imaging and raise phototoxicity, the light damage to samples. Their structured detection microscope reshapes how emitted light spreads, moving signal away from the noisiest parts of the image. That sharpens sensitivity to emitter pairs closer than the diffraction limit, in two dimensions, with no mode-sorting optics. The team shows it working on fluorophores attached to DNA nanorulers.
arxiv-2604-00613: Mohammadamini and colleagues present KUTED, a speech-to-text translation dataset for Central Kurdish built from TED and TEDx talks. The corpus holds 91,000 sentence pairs, with 170 hours of English audio and over a million tokens in each language. Tests show spelling variation badly hurts Kurdish translation, yielding nonstandard outputs. A systematic standardisation approach lifts performance and yields steadier translations. On a held-out test set, a fine-tuned Seamless model scores 15.18 BLEU, and the standardisation improves the Seamless baseline by 3 BLEU on the FLEURS benchmark.
arxiv-2604-00913: Liu and team build IKEA-Bench, a set of 1,623 questions in 6 task types on 29 IKEA products, to assess vision-language models on cross-drawing building guide matching. Testing 19 models from 2B to 38B under three matching plans, they find building grasp is won back via text. Yet text harms diagram-to-video matching, and design predicts scores better than size. Video grasp stays a hard block no matter the plan, and diagrams and video live in their own visual spaces.
arxiv-2604-01013: Altangerel and team report the sighting of magneto-chiral anisotropy in ultrasound sent along and across alpha-quartz. They built an ultrasound device sharp to around 10^-8 in velocity ratio. They also present a simple large-scale Becquerel-like math model that fits the effect's size and how it varies with frequency.
arxiv-2604-01113: Liu and colleagues introduce MIMIC-DOS, a dataset for organ dysfunction worsening prediction in intensive care, built from cases where symptoms clash with signs. Single-pass models and agentic pipelines struggle to reconcile conflicting signals, so CARE, a privacy-compliant agentic design, is proposed. A proprietary model guides by generating categories and transitions without touching patient data, while a local model uses them for evidence and decisions. In tests on MIMIC-DOS, CARE beats the language models and agentic workflows across metrics, handling conflicting evidence better while preserving privacy.
arxiv-2604-01213: Rubio and colleagues present a joint planning method for mixed robot teams on other worlds. Old planners slow down fast as pairings and routes grow, so the team uses Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization, which moves the hard scaling work from run time to training time. It assigns tasks and schedules to get the most science from each robot's own skills. Tests compare it with exhaustive-search best results and try live replanning on a planet mission.
arxiv-2604-01313: Xia and colleagues warn that the usual training loss for conditional flow matching can stall early while physical accuracy keeps improving. Using Jefferson Lab scattering data and synthetic stress tests, they show physics-aware scores still climb long after the standard loss flattens. A single loss number can thus hide real progress in generative simulation. Their answer is ScatterPrism, a generative surrogate judged by a set of physics checks meant to ensure true motion fidelity without rote recall, aimed first at the coming Electron-Ion Collider.
arxiv-2604-01413: Zhou and colleagues ask when a language model should stop. Simple rules and turn budgets answer without guarantees. Conformal prediction offers coverage guarantees, but methods handle only a single output, not pipelines with stopping. Their Multi-Turn Conformal Prediction system splits budgets across turns, letting the model stop early while keeping a coverage guarantee. Shown on retrieval-augmented generation and ReAct, it hits its targets on single-hop and multi-hop benchmarks. It reduces turns, compute cost and set size. They also offer a metric scoring validity and speed.
arxiv-2604-01713: Paliathanasis tests whether a generalized uncertainty principle, which implies a smallest possible length, leaves traces in cosmic structure. A modified bracket yields a changed equation for the standard Lambda-CDM model and a one-parameter dark energy picture. Using growth measures from redshift-space distortions plus background data on Type Ia supernovae, baryon acoustic oscillations and cosmic chronometers, the fit finds a negative deformation parameter. The standard model limit still sits inside the 95 percent credible interval, and evidence gives weak to strong support depending on the data set.
arxiv-2604-01813: Barkatou presents new classes of open sets in two- or three-dimensional real space, defined by a geometric property tied to the inward normal. The focus is proving compactness for the Hausdorff topology within these classes. The paper also shows that Hausdorff, compact, and characteristic-function convergence coincide for select classes. It further studies how smooth the thickness function is for these domains, and how smoothness of a fixed convex set affects boundary smoothness of the allowed shapes.
arxiv-2604-01913: Wu and colleagues explain plasticity loss in reinforcement learning, the fading ability to keep adapting. They trace it to shifting inputs and shifting targets from bootstrapping, pinning it to rank collapse in the neural tangent kernel Gram matrix and shrinking gradient size. Existing fixes address the first mechanism, so the team targets the second with Sample Weight Decay, restoring gradient size. Tests on TD3, Double DQN and SAC with SimBa across MuJoCo, ALE and DeepMind Control tasks eased plasticity loss and lifted learning, reaching top humanoid scores.
arxiv-2604-02013: Galviz constructs the functional integral for Abelian Chern-Simons theory with a toral gauge group at level K, where K is an even symmetric bilinear form, integral and nondegenerate. Exact zeta Gaussian evaluation of the quotient sum over connections modulo gauge gives the whole build. For closed 3-manifolds the result is a topological invariant, and for manifolds with boundary the sum yields the edge state. This new theory meets the axioms of a (2+1)-dimensional quantum field theory.
arxiv-2604-02113: Zhuang, Yoo, Luo, Guo and Zhang question how steering vectors for language model reasoning get built. Keyword hunting in thought traces, they find, marks boundaries that mostly fail to reproduce the same behavior when regenerated, diluting the steering signal. Their stability filter keeps only boundaries that behave consistently, and a content subspace projection strips question specific noise. The filtered vectors score 0.784 on MATH-500 and transfer across models in the same family without fresh extraction.
arxiv-2604-02313: Ferko and team extend neural network field theory to topological settings. Discrete labels mark the quantum number in the new frame. The frame yields the Berezinskii Kosterlitz Thouless transition, including the spin wave critical line and vortex proliferation at high heat. It also checks T-duality of the bosonic string: invariance under momentum and winding exchange and Buscher rules for sigma model couplings on toroidal backgrounds. Current algebra boost at self dual radius and non geometric T-fold functions round out the check.
arxiv-2604-02513: Balaji and three colleagues unify sparse Bayesian learning, a popular way to recover sparse signals, under the majorization-minimization principle. They show the leading algorithms are descent steps for a shared majorizer, which yields new convergence guarantees and a wider family of methods. Going further, they train a neural network to learn a better update rule from data, and it beats the classical methods across varied recovery problems.
arxiv-2604-02613: Proudkii and ten colleagues survey gases escaping from disrupting comet Leonard before its closest approach to the Sun, using the NOEMA and APEX telescopes. They firmly detect hydrogen cyanide and carbon monosulfide, with upper limits on methanol, formaldehyde and carbon monoxide. Carbon monosulfide levels relative to water rise about fivefold as the comet nears the Sun, which fits a spread-out source, while hydrogen cyanide stays near the nucleus.
arxiv-2604-02713: Deng and three colleagues probe how chatbots break down in chats that are charged with feeling and fraught with ethics. Prior work leans on static safety checks, missing how alignment unfolds over turns. With a simulator that plays users with set personas and staged emotional pacing, they find breakdowns that worsen as feelings escalate. Empathy at times overrides duty, and ethical guidance fails. They sort the patterns into a taxonomy with design lessons.
arxiv-2604-02813: Pasic and four colleagues study co-locating sub-6 GHz and millimeter-wave antenna arrays for future wireless systems, where sub-6 GHz information can aid millimeter-wave links. Both arrays must sit together and align precisely to share multipath effects, but placing one in front of the other may distort radiation patterns. Simulations and measurements show the millimeter-wave structure barely affects sub-6 GHz performance, so co-location is feasible.
arxiv-2604-03013: Bronasco and colleagues explain a puzzling accuracy jump in spectral deferred correction, a step-by-step solver for differential equations. They show accuracy can rise by two orders in one round, not just one, when errors use certain inconsistent, implicit discretizations that allow parallel work. They also find such methods usually fall back to explicit Runge-Kutta stability, so future designs must balance the gain against that cost.
arxiv-2604-03313: Jain builds CardioSAM, a heart MRI segmentation tool that pairs a frozen Segment Anything encoder with a light, heart-specific decoder. The decoder adds an attention module using heart topology priors and a boundary module that sharpens tissue edges. On the ACDC benchmark it reaches a Dice score near 93 percent, beating nnU-Net by about 4 points and topping expert agreement levels.
arxiv-2604-03713: Piyush Agrawal and Manish Agrawal designed lattice shapes whose geometry changes bit by bit, rather than in jumps, to hit a chosen goal. Lattices built from a grid of struts can be made stronger or lighter by grading their thickness, but standard search methods produced abrupt jumps that focus stress at weak spots. The pair wove Gaussian random functions and Gaussian process regression into the search, with a projection step that keeps each design smooth. Test cases yielded smooth designs that still met their goals while spreading stress more evenly.
arxiv-2604-04113: Elmar Biernat and Alfred Stadler gave the first calculation of tensor and axial-tensor mesons with total spin at least 2 in Covariant Spectator Theory. A refined quark-antiquark interaction kernel now carries the momentum dependence of the strong coupling, replacing a constant kernel term. Global least-squares fits to established heavy and heavy-light meson masses described the spectrum for spins 0, 1, 2, and 3 parities with only eight adjustable parameters. The fit quality was excellent across the full spin-parity set.
arxiv-2604-04313: Nasybullin and Kurkin apply computer vision and neural networks to sort brain activity from EEG traces during hand movement. They clean raw EEG signals and turn them into two-dimensional topograms, maps of brain activity across the scalp. Supervised and semi-supervised networks then sort motor cortex activities. The paper frames the work as a step toward better EEG analysis in neuroscience.
arxiv-2604-04413: Hong, Park and Kim survey robust deep joint source-channel coding for semantic message systems, where only task-essential information is sent. Deep joint source-channel coding promises much for such systems, yet it falters when live channels differ from training ones, making toughness vital. The survey groups recent toughness methods into robust training and tunable methods, the latter splitting into tunable semantic feature picks, hardware-layer tweaks and semantic feature tweaks. Finally, the authors discuss promising paths including multi-task generalization and explainability in robust semantic systems.
arxiv-2604-04613: Dwivedi and Rupp propose a hybridized discontinuous Galerkin method for the Einstein-scalar system. After rewriting the model as a local first-order PDE-ODE system, they build a semidiscrete scheme with local unknowns and coupling through mesh traces. In this radial setting, traces can be eliminated recursively, so only the main variable advances in time. The authors prove local well-posedness. They establish an optimal L2 error bound for the main evolution variable. They also obtain reconstruction error estimates for metric variables. Tests verify the predicted convergence rate.
arxiv-2604-05213: Rosado-Marín and colleagues constrain non-Gaussianity with correlations of DESI DR1 tracers, using LRGs, QSOs, and ELGs at redshift 1 to 3. Cross-checking across tracers tests systematics, since cross-correlations resist non-common systematics. Cross-correlation improves f_NL by about 9 percent, to 2, minus 8, plus 9, at 68 percent confidence. Including the ELG sample gives no clear improvement. Mock tests predict an additional 8 percent gain with scatter, and the lack of data improvement fits that expectation. The project explores DESI ELG clustering for f_NL, ahead of DESI analyses.
arxiv-2604-05813: Bąk, Garbulińska-Węgrzyn, and Popławski study universal ultrahomogeneous 1-Lipschitz retractions on the Urysohn space. They introduce extension rule UR-star, matching universality plus ultrahomogeneity, plus a pointwise retract topology for these maps. The paper probes Borel complexity and density of the special retractions among all 1-Lipschitz retractions on the space.
arxiv-2604-05913: Lahtinen and Koulouri survey Bayesian solvers for EEG source imaging, which maps brain activity from scalp sensors. They compare Gaussian, Laplace, and group Laplace priors, with focus on sparse hierarchical models, and spell out expectation-maximization and alternating optimization builds. Depth-weighted priors built on a signal-to-noise frame cut depth bias, and simulations show prior choice shapes how well deep sources are found.
arxiv-2604-06013: Cuccarese proposes epistemic blinding, a 2026 check on model analysis that swaps named entities for anonymous codes before prompting and compares the result with an unblinded control. The aim is to expose how much of an answer comes from supplied data rather than memory. In oncology drug-target ranking across four cancer types, blinding changed 16 percent of top-20 predictions while still recovering the validated targets. In equity screening, brand-recognition bias reshaped 30 to 40 percent of top-20 rankings, and the protocol is released as an open-source tool.
arxiv-2604-06113: Dahmani and seven colleagues generate large outdoor driving scenes with a diffusion model guided by semantic voxel grids. Each occupied voxel in their Sigma-Voxfield grid stores a fixed set of colored surface samples, and the model works over local voxel neighborhoods with three-dimensional positional codes. Overlapping regions are painted outward step by step to reach large areas, then a deferred rendering module turns the grid into photorealistic images. The result stays consistent across viewpoints without optimizing each scene separately, at moderate cost versus existing methods.
arxiv-2604-06413: Xiao Shou proposes Optimal Transport Neural Flow Matching, an ODE-free framework for direct maps. Diffusion and flow matching need tens to hundreds of evaluations at inference. Neural flows parameterize the flow map, enabling generation in one forward pass. Naive training suffers mean collapse, where inconsistent pairings push every output toward the data mean. The author proves consistent coupling necessary for non-degenerate learning, addressed with optimal transport pairings using minibatch and online coupling. Synthetic benchmarks, MNIST, and CIFAR-10 show competitive quality with a single network evaluation.
arxiv-2604-06613: Wang and Zhu show reasoning models often know the answer long before they stop talking. Across five setups, two model families, and three benchmarks, 52 to 88 percent of chain-of-thought tokens come after the answer is already recoverable. Free continuations from early prefixes recover the answer even at a tenth of the trace, while forced extraction fails in 42 percent of such cases. Their Black-box Adaptive Early Exit method cuts 70 to 78 percent of serial generation while lifting accuracy, using free continuations to spot and pull out the answer.
arxiv-2604-06813: Aznar, Pujol, and Díez coordinate robot swarms through event-triggered adaptive consensus. Swarm task allocation in shifting, bandwidth-tight settings challenges group smarts. Their framework opens task talks only on big events, lets the swarm tune its pace to local conflict, and keeps agents tough through Behavior Trees. Tests benchmark it against non-talking reactive moves, simple sharing, baseline and periodic CBBA variants, and C-CBBA. Results show lower network load with top-tier tasks done and strong toughness against failed runs and lost agents.
arxiv-2604-07013: Maleki, Marchisio, and Shafique present QNAS, a search tool that designs quantum neural nets able to run on near term noisy hardware. Hand built quantum circuits must juggle power, train skill, and scarce qubits, and cutting large circuits adds steep cost. QNAS trains one shared super circuit and uses a multi goal search to weigh test error, run time, and the count of cut pieces under a qubit cap. The best handwriting net tops ninety seven percent with a small eight qubit circuit.
arxiv-2604-07113: Tomalak offers a solo paper on radiative corrections from virtual pions in inverse beta decay, the main way reactor and supernova antineutrinos are caught. Precise cross sections at antineutrino energies above ten mega electron volts need these small quantum tweaks worked out. Using heavy baryon chiral perturbation theory, the author finds that at leading order only pion isospin breaking terms escape suppression by the electron mass. At next order, besides recoil effects, only one Wilson coefficient shapes the energy trend, yet its exact value barely matters at low energies.
arxiv-2604-07213: Kawasaki-Borruat and three colleagues show how to set up diffusion on data shapes using only scattered points. Their method, called implicit manifold-valued diffusions, builds random-motion rules in the full high-dimensional space. The motion stays on the hidden low-dimensional shape, guided by a graph of near points. As more points arrive, the discrete motion tends to its smooth form, and tests on toy shapes and MNIST show it stays on the shape and aids guided search.
arxiv-2604-07313: Girdhar and three colleagues construct a helical three-dimensional second-order topological superconductor from weakly coupled Rashba nanowires. They find a regime where bulk and surface spectra are both gapped, yet a pair of helical parafermionic modes stays gapless along a closed loop of one-dimensional hinges. The hinge path follows the hierarchy of interwire couplings and how the sample ends. In the noninteracting limit, the system instead hosts gapless Majorana hinge modes, linking the exotic parafermionic case to a familiar topological phase.
arxiv-2604-07413: Jian and 15 colleagues introduce FORGE, a fine-grained multimodal test for manufacturing settings. Current tests miss factory rigor, hampered by scarce data and weak domain semantics. FORGE pairs real 2D images with 3D point clouds annotated with fine details like exact model numbers, then tests 18 leading multimodal models on three tasks. Visual grounding is not the main bottleneck; missing domain knowledge is. Tuning a compact 3-billion-parameter model on FORGE data lifts held-out accuracy by up to 90.8 percent relatively.
arxiv-2604-07613: Zhu and three colleagues use 20-parsec wind tunnel simulations to pin down when ram pressure stripping stops quenching dwarf satellites. The simulations add radiative cooling in a multiphase medium, star formation, and stellar feedback, varying satellite masses and host gas densities. Stripping matches the McCarthy et al. 2008 analytic prediction. Star formation quenches fast when stripping works, but can briefly rise or reignite when stripping is partial. Stripping works below about 10 million solar masses in stars but fails above it, a threshold 0.5 to 1 dex below observations and cosmological simulations.
arxiv-2604-07813: Yan and Gašević propose Agentivism, a learning theory for an age when AI can do learners' work for them. Strong assisted performance no longer proves learning, since students may finish tasks well while gaining little lasting understanding. Agentivism frames learning as lasting growth in human skill through selective delegation, careful checking of AI contributions, rebuilding assisted work from within, and transferring skill once support is withdrawn. The theory explains how learning stays possible when delegation is easy and constant.
arxiv-2604-08013: El Bachraoui proves Andrews' Conjectures 5 and 6 on the coefficients of v1(q). Folsom, Males, Rolen, and Storzer lately proved Conjecture 4 and a refined density-one version of the third for the same series. The new proof studies the trigonometric factor's simple zeros in the earlier authors' asymptotic formula. It shows the key quadratic sequence keeps a positive distance from whole numbers infinitely often. The argument is unconditional, requiring no unproven hypotheses. It completes two more cases of Andrews' claims on this q-series.
arxiv-2604-08113: Halder, Sadhukhan, and Palit propose TADP-RME, a trust-adaptive differential privacy framework for reliable data-driven systems. Privacy must anchor systems in adversarial settings, yet existing schemes use a fixed privacy budget, creating a rigid utility-privacy tradeoff that fails under heterogeneous user trust. Noise-only differential privacy also preserves geometric structure, which inference attacks exploit to leak privacy. TADP-RME introduces an inverse trust score between 0 and 1 to modulate the privacy budget adaptively, enabling smooth transitions between utility and privacy. Reverse Manifold Embedding adds a further structural defense.
arxiv-2604-08213: Wang and 11 colleagues present EditCaption for image editing instructions. Good source-target pairs with exact editing instructions matter for instruction-guided editing, yet building triplets at scale stays costly. Recent pipelines use vision-language models to synthesize editing instructions, but strong models still struggle to describe visual changes between pairs. They show three repeated failure types: mixed-up orientation, unclear viewpoint, and missing details. Human review of 400 pairs found several open-source baselines with critical-error rates above 47 percent, leaving many synthesized instructions unfit for training.
arxiv-2604-08713: Yabesi and three colleagues use eye tracking to study how urgency and status shape developers' trust in reused code. In a controlled experiment with 37 developers, patch priority changed review time, mental load, and perceived quality. Author seniority shifted visual scanning patterns, yet neither changed the final decision to adopt code or measured performance. Participants named features, quality, and clarity as their main criteria, overlooking urgency and status effects on their own choices.
arxiv-2604-08913: Kazma and Taha connect probability models that favour varied selections with the mathematics of sensor and actuator choice in linear control systems. They show that observability and controllability Gramians, which measure how well sensors observe and actuators steer a system, behave as determinantal point processes. This gives a probabilistic view of which nodes to pick. The paper proves inclusion and diversity properties, recovers greedy selection guarantees, and tests the theory on three network layouts.
arxiv-2604-09213: Konovalova, Kuznetsov, and Alanov propose SHIFT, a light framework for removing unwanted concepts from diffusion transformer image models at inference time. SHIFT learns steering vectors for chosen layers and steps that suppress a target concept while keeping the rest of the prompt and image quality intact. The same steering can push generations toward a desired style or bias samples toward adding or changing target objects. Tests across varied prompts show flexible control, offering a fast way to edit model behavior after training.
arxiv-2604-09413: Hutiri, Scheuerman, Nagpal, Hoag, and Xiang argue one-size-fits-all consent for creative works in AI is too weak. Real ownership setups, style copying, and endless use contexts make binary opt-in by default fail. The authors examine control levers at training, inference, and sharing, putting inference-time opt-in forward as a missed chance for nuanced checks. They propose an agent-based inference-time design checking whether user intent meets rights-holder terms, shown in a music case study.
arxiv-2604-10213: Anand, Lohani, Mishra, and Pandey adapt LiDAR data across sensors and weather with ReaLiTy, a physics-based method. Current data sets rarely show the same scene under different sensors and weather. ReaLiTy remakes LiDAR data to target sensors and weather, blending real cues with a learning module for true brightness. A physics-based weather model adds shape and radiometric damage. The LiDAR Adaptation Dataset Suite offers change-ready point clouds matched with sources. Tests show better match and true weather effects, a shared base for LiDAR tuning.
arxiv-2604-10413: Manabe, Shibata, Takamichi, and Aoki carry sign language feeling straight into spoken voice. Turning signs into plain text first drops the non verbal color that signing holds. Their new task, sign to speech prosody transfer, keeps global tone and stress in the spoken result. SignRecGAN trains from single mode sets with no paired sign speech labels, using adversarial training and rebuild losses. Tests show the speech mirrors the signed mood, and the team plans open code.
arxiv-2604-10513: David, Fournier, Limonad, and Mulian fix agent prompts without paying for fresh rollouts. Vague prompts send one agent down split paths with split results. Standard tuning pays twice: once to draft prompts, once to score them. Their SFA pipeline reads old traces, groups node outputs, and ranks meaning traits with a decision tree. Surviving traits enter the prompt as fixes, beating tuned rivals most where rollouts cost most.
arxiv-2604-10613: Arushi and Kumar introduce the first conformal finite-element framework for nonlinear collisional breakage equations. They describe how particles shatter when they hit each other, a process found across science and engineering. Earlier methods struggled in two and three dimensions, where moment sums, stability, and speed all grow harder. Their scheme pairs high-order Lagrange elements with BDF2 time steps and keeps total particle count and volume intact. Tests in one, two, and three dimensions show high accuracy and optimal convergence.
arxiv-2604-10913: Kiriki and three colleagues show that Lyapunov exponents can fail to exist throughout a dense subset of the Newhouse domain of surface maps. For any map in that subset, exponents fail for all points in some open set and every nonzero tangent vector in some open cone. This makes non-existence a persistent phenomenon under robust homoclinic tangencies, not an isolated quirk. The proof builds maps with particular oscillatory return times near a homoclinic tangency, using Newhouse theory and recent work on Lyapunov irregularity.
arxiv-2604-11313: Adhikary explores engineered non-Gaussian coherence as a fuel for quantum batteries. Building on his earlier scheme for generating non-Gaussian states, he tests how coherence in those states can lift battery performance across Gaussian charger profiles under unitary dynamics. Thermal broadening and environmental coupling to the charger are also examined as levers for stable performance under careful thermal management. In plain terms, the work asks whether quantum quirks can store and release energy better. The study is a proof of concept for using thermodynamic resources in quantum energy storage.
arxiv-2604-11813: Dossou-Olory, Andriantiana, Rakotonarivo, and Shozi study a ratio between two counts for a graph. The first counts one-nearly independent vertex subsets; the second is the Merrifield-Simmons index, which counts zero-nearly independent subsets. Building on earlier comparisons of these two quantities, they establish sharp lower and upper bounds for their ratio. Those bounds cover connected graphs, trees, and forests.
arxiv-2604-12513: Yves Ruffenach asks whether a language model can control itself from internal evidence. His model pairs local variational computation with a regulator that holds inner states steady. Checkpoint retention keeps useful past states. A controller uses uncertainty as a live signal, not just an after-the-fact readout. Uncertainty then steers training, retention, and inference-time action. The backbone beats a matched plain rival on language tasks. Its controller stays active with a favorable balance of quality and cost.
arxiv-2604-12613: Michal Czakon and three colleagues compute photon-pair production at next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order in QCD. Two isolated photons at the Large Hadron Collider matter for Higgs studies and new-physics searches. Percent-level theory would sharpen those measurements. This first N3LO calculation tests whether perturbation theory converges. It also shrinks theory error threefold, down to 3 percent. The result paves the way to improved analyses.
arxiv-2604-12813: Xinyue Li and five colleagues split video quality work into perception and calibration. Pretrained multimodal models already sense quality, but tuning them to new scenes costs heavy retraining. DPC-VQA freezes a multimodal model for a base score and adds a light branch for a residual fix. The split avoids full retraining and keeps performance reliable. On user-made and AI-made benchmarks, it matches strong baselines. It uses under 2 percent of standard parameters and stays effective with only 20 percent of labels.
arxiv-2604-13113: Abdullah extends the sigma index, the overall variance of a graph's degree sequence, to fuzzy graphs. She defines the fuzzy sigma index from fuzzy vertex degrees and fuzzy graph size, then proves its basic properties, including sharp lower and upper bounds. She also analyzes how the index behaves under standard fuzzy graph operations, laying a foundation for further work on variance-based topological indices in fuzzy graph theory.
arxiv-2604-13313: Im, Madhwal, and Gupta improve compositional understanding in vision-language models by mining harder contrastive negatives. Their ConcretePlant method targets highly concrete words, whose changes create sharper visual and structural contrasts, and their Cement loss uses a margin to rebalance gradients that easy pairs otherwise dominate. The combined Slipform framework reaches state-of-the-art accuracy across compositional benchmarks and also strengthens general cross-modal retrieval and linear probing.
arxiv-2604-13413: Fang and seven colleagues show that dataset-level metrics hide non-determinism in diffusion language models. Averaging sample quality across runs makes setups with similar total scores look alike, even when single inputs behave very differently. Their fine-grained evaluation tracks sample differences across guidance scale, diffusion steps, Monte Carlo sampling, batch size, and hardware. That spread proves widespread and structured, with code generation far more sensitive than question answering. Their Factor Variance Attribution metric splits observed spread across factor settings.
arxiv-2604-13913: Luo and Zhang prove the Hausdorff dimension of the graph of a random vector-valued Weierstrass function, built from cosine and sine series with random phase shifts. The dimension equals the smaller of two values set by the series' growth and decay rates, holding with probability one. Their result pins down the roughness of a jagged curve whose wiggles repeat at ever finer scales.
arxiv-2604-14113: Tang and colleagues make GUI grounding zoom adaptively instead of uniformly. UI-Zoomer treats both the zoom trigger and the zoom scale as uncertainty problems: a confidence gate blends agreement across random candidates with token-level confidence, firing only when localization is uncertain. An uncertainty-driven crop module then sizes each crop from prediction variance. Gains reach up to 13.4 percent across ScreenSpot-Pro, UI-Vision, and ScreenSpot-v2, with no extra training.
arxiv-2604-14213: Baddis and four colleagues run CUDA codes with Hamilton-Jacobi methods to study shadows of rotating charged Euler-Heisenberg black holes threaded by global monopoles. Shadow shape and energy emission both track the monopole strength, the electric charge, and the spin, while the Euler-Heisenberg nonlinear factor barely moves either. To square theory with Event Horizon Telescope shadow observations, the team uses its CUDA computations to set tight bounds. The bounds cover the monopole factor, the charge, and the spin.
arxiv-2604-14913: Banagl studies equivariant L-classes of Atiyah-Singer-Zagier type for singular spaces. If a finite group acts on a rational homology manifold, the orbit space is again one, but more singular spaces need care. He proves that when the G-space is a Witt pseudomanifold, including all singular complex pure-dimensional varieties, the orbit space is again one. In the compact oriented case this gives Goresky-MacPherson L-classes, and he builds equivariant ones computing the orbit space class through an averaging formula.
arxiv-2604-15013: Koh and four others present DEX-Mouse, a portable calibration-free interface with force feedback, built from off-the-shelf parts under 150 dollars. Dexterous hand manipulation needs large-scale consistent demonstrations, but simulation, video, and glove methods suffer sim-to-real gaps or per-operator calibration. The operator-agnostic design needs no calibration or change, and forearm mounting yields robot-aligned data. In user tests, the attached setup reached 86.67 percent completion and reduced workload versus separated setups. Hardware, software, bill of materials and firmware are open-sourced.
arxiv-2604-15113: Snyder and colleagues present HyperSpace, a modular framework for spatial coding in hyperdimensional vector systems. It splits vector symbolic architectures into plug-in operators. Encoding, binding, and bundling join similarity, cleanup, and regression as separate modules. Tests on two backends show similarity and cleanup dominate run time in spatial tasks, leaving the two systems roughly even end to end. Memory use differs, though, with HRR needing about half the memory of FHRR vectors.
arxiv-2604-15413: Igoshin and seven colleagues adapt the optical theorem, which ties a scatterer's extinction cross section to how strongly it scatters forward, to acoustics. Their method survives real-world limits such as finite sources, weak scattered signals, and imperfect echo-free rooms. On a Helmholtz resonator, it finds one strong resonance near 2000 Hz whose place, height, and shape match full-wave simulations.
arxiv-2604-15513: Chen and three colleagues present Divide and Truncate, a unified scheme coupling multi-physics systems through penetration-free contact handling across rigid bodies, soft volumes, thin shells, rods, and animated objects. Space is split into separate zones, and moves are cut short to stay in their zone, which ensures contact with no penetration. A planar variant restricts only motion toward nearby surfaces, fixing artificial damping and deadlock while staying material- and solver-agnostic.
arxiv-2604-15613: Silva presents Green-ELM, a non-iterative neural design that swaps gradient-based output training for a closed-form analytic solve over fixed random features. Projecting inputs into a high-dimensional random feature space untangles complex class boundaries without backpropagation. With Moore-Penrose, LU, and Cholesky solves, it hits 98.10 percent on MNIST and 86.63 percent on Fashion-MNIST, training 11.6 times faster than an SGD baseline on CPU.
arxiv-2604-15713: Kappelmann and five colleagues study full, lean type tags for rank-one polymorphic lambda terms as used in Isabelle, building on Smolka, Blanchette, and co-workers. They give a full formal spec with proofs, all built in Isabelle/HOL. A human and an LLM agent each draft pen-and-paper proofs on their own, and the agent turns both into Isabelle form, with human hints honing and widening the work.
arxiv-2604-15913: Minotti and Modanese apply the fluctuation-dissipation theorem to Aharonov-Bohm electrodynamics, which unlike Maxwell theory allows local non-conservation of charge. For non-conserved charges at thermal equilibrium, they recover the same spectral energy distribution as Maxwell theory. The electric share of that energy doubles, however, while the magnetic share matches Maxwell, with the excess balanced by a negative term from the Aharonov-Bohm scalar field. For a conductor described by the gamma model, they derive a current correlation spectrum adding violet noise to classical Johnson-Nyquist white noise.
arxiv-2604-16213: Frazier, Damevski, and Pollock study conversational agents for secondary students learning AP Computer Science Principles. Students often turn to web tutorials and question sites, but struggle to find material matched to their task and background. The authors compare general chat agents with custom fixed-response agents built for CSP students, using classroom trials with 45 high school students across six sections, and assess help, effectiveness, and engagement.
arxiv-2604-16313: Wu and ten colleagues present MARA, a framework for answering questions over documents with text and images. Current methods use query-blind document views and a fixed top-k choice of proof. They miss salient content, and fail when relevant proof spreads unevenly. MARA adapts both finding and writing to the query. A region encoder reweights multi-level document views by query fit. A proof controller checks whether proof is enough during writing, and adjusts the choice as needed.
